description: ​We are a team of developers who love 3D graphics, coding, and space science. Our goal is simple: take complex, hard-to-read NASA radar data and turn it into an interactive 3D web app that anyone can explore and understand in real time
summary: CHRONO-SAR turns NASA's NISAR radar data into ground you can watch move. NISAR measures millimetre-scale ground motion every 12 days, but its products are multi-gigabyte HDF5 files of phase "rainbows" that only radar experts can read. Our app runs in a single browser tab. It queries NASA's catalogue (CMR) live, selects the NISAR products that fit the need (the whole place covered, the newest pass, 12-day pairs, validated products first) and lays their real values on real 3D elevation models: interferometric phase, line-of-sight change, coherence and calibrated L-band backscatter. Every pixel shows height, motion and surface together. Six places tell the story: Mount Rainier, the San Andreas Fault, Jakobshavn Glacier, a flooded forest in Louisiana, the Danube Delta and sinking Mexico City. Clearly labelled physics simulations explain the radar and let us test algorithms that run live in the browser, such as phase unwrapping with 4.3 mm error. It matters because civil protection, planners and students can finally see what the radar already measures, with no GIS, no login.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

CHRONO-SAR is a 4D NISAR "Earth-motion engine" that runs in one browser tab. Radar interferometry measures millimetres of ground motion, but the result is a rainbow of phase fringes that only specialists can read. CHRONO-SAR feeds the radar phase into the terrain itself (Δd = λ/4π · Δφ), so the ground visibly moves. Six real places show four kinds of motion: Mount Rainier (volcano), the San Andreas Fault, Jakobshavn Glacier, the Atchafalaya Basin and the Danube Delta (floods under vegetation), and Mexico City (subsidence).

HOW IT WORKS: THE DATA

- Real NISAR data: for every scene the app queries NASA's Common Metadata Repository (CMR) live and lists the real NISAR products over it, the latest pass and the archive inventory.

- Selection criteria, tied to the need: the product must cover the whole place, be the newest pass, be a 12-day pair (so the phase stays coherent), and validated products come before provisional ones.

- We downloaded seven NISAR products from ASF DAAC: six GUNW interferograms (one per scene) and one GCOV polarimetric product. A Python tool reads the HDF5 files, projects them onto each scene's grid (UTM and polar stereographic, implemented ourselves) and stores the real wrapped and unwrapped phase, line-of-sight change, coherence, pixel offsets and calibrated HH/HV backscatter.

- Where the data goes: every value lands on the same 384 × 384 grid as a real elevation model (USGS 3DEP, SRTM, Copernicus DEM), so one pixel holds height, motion and surface together. Press R to drape NISAR's real measurement on the 3D terrain and read the measured values under the cursor.

- Physics-based simulations, always labelled SIMULATED, cover a full year of 29 passes with a known truth, so we can explain the radar and test our algorithms.

FEATURES

L-band and S-band, an "X-ray lens" that compares them, phase / 3D deformation / Freeman–Durden polarimetry / coherence views, ascending, descending and 3D-fusion geometry, live quality-guided phase unwrapping (4.3 mm error against truth), coherence change detection (finds a 6.2 km² debris flow vs 5.6 km² in the model), an on-demand Mw 7.9 fault rupture, cross-sections, a 2D/3D split view, a detailed NISAR spacecraft model with its deployment, a self-running jury tour, and Excel/CSV export with an explanation for every dataset.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Civil protection, city planners, teachers and students can see where and how fast the ground moves without GIS software, a login or radar expertise. The NASA catalogue query works for any place on Earth, and the converter reads any NISAR GUNW or GCOV file, so the approach scales beyond our six scenes.

CREATIVITY

Instead of another map viewer, CHRONO-SAR makes the radar phase move the ground in 3D and lets you ask any pixel what the satellite measured. It puts simulation (to understand) and real NISAR data (to trust) side by side, clearly labelled.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Data honesty (every view says REAL or SIMULATED; the app states that a 12-day pair mixes ground motion with atmosphere, and that the product does not document its toward/away sign convention), accuracy (georeferencing checked against coastlines and lakes), and performance (multi-gigabyte products reduced to about 0.6 MB per scene).

TOOLS

JavaScript (ES modules), three.js 0.160, hand-written WebGL 2 GLSL shaders, Canvas 2D, Web Audio, ExcelJS; Node.js for the build and local server; Python with NumPy, h5py and Pillow for the data tools. Data: NASA CMR, ASF DAAC (NISAR L2 GUNW and GCOV), AWS Terrain Tiles, Copernicus DEM GLO-90. Hardware: a standard laptop; it runs in any browser with WebGL 2.
